text:
Rhea Iyer: quick sync - we need a migration story for assertion envelopes across hosted -> dedicated -> private. current multi-header approach breaks routing.
Marco Diaz: Agreed. We should define a single canonical envelope and a compatibility shim for older services.
Ivy Patel: Important: streaming RPCs are sensitive. Long-lived streams shouldn't force re-signing for every token refresh. How do we bind assertions to a connection?
Sam Brooks: Idea: keep per-request envelope for control-plane calls, and a connection-bound mutable token for streams. Connection token references an active assertion id (aid) and a short-lived proof.
Rhea Iyer: Example header proposal (compact):
```
X-RW-Authz: v=1;fmt=compact;pl=eyJ0aWQiOiJzZW50IiwgImFpZCI6IjU2NyIsICJmbGFncyI6WyJuby1sb2ciXX0=;alg=hs256;sig=ab12cd...
```
Marco Diaz: Compatibility: shim should accept old headers and synthesize canonical envelope. We must be explicit about priority rules if both exist.
Ivy Patel: Security: adapters must not upgrade privileges. Add an explicit "mapping_policy" that lists allowed flag translations. Also require adapters to include mapping_reason in audit events.
Sam Brooks: Operational: private adapter could run a local verifier that validates platform-signed envelopes via a short-lived TLS mTLS channel to control plane, or validate customer KMS-signed tokens locally. If control plane is unreachable, adapter should fall back to local policy and emit a degraded-audit event.
Rhea Iyer: Migration plan ideas: 1) publish verifier libs and shims, 2) runtime accepts both old and new headers for 8 weeks, preferring new envelope when present, 3) adapter shim logs translation counts and failures, 4) tenant-by-tenant roll with opt-in flag.
Marco Diaz: For streams, use a connection-binding header X-RW-Conn that references an aid and a small proof. Proof can be rotated without tearing down streams (so proxies refresh proof every 60s).
Ivy Patel: Testing: add fuzz tests to eval that simulate reordered, duplicated, and truncated envelopes. Also add a negative test: adapter attempts to drop "no-log" must be rejected by verifier.
Sam Brooks: Telemetry: span tags should include aid and adapter_translation=true|false. Do NOT log the full payload. Also produce a metric for "translation_mismatch".
Rhea Iyer: Rollout knobs: per-tenant permissive-mode (accept platform-signed fallback) vs strict-mode (reject unverifiable). Default to permissive for 2 weeks then strict.
Marco Diaz: Who rotates platform signing keys? Control plane. We'll publish rotation windows and a JWKS endpoint for verifiers. Private deployments can cache JWKS or use adapter handshake to fetch allowed keys.
Ivy Patel: One more: support an "orig_assertion_hash" field allowed in adapter audit so we can correlate post-translation without exposing payload.
deploy-bot: Created task #MAINT-4829 in hosting-handbook: "Canonical assertion envelope + migration plan" assigned to @Rhea Iyer and @Marco Diaz.
Rhea Iyer: Actions: I'll draft the migration RFC (header grammar, stream binding, rollout windows). Marco will prototype shims and JWKS flow. Ivy + Sam will add tests and audit schema. Target: staging canary in 4 weeks.
Marco Diaz: ack. I'll include a tiny Go verifier and Node shim for adapters.
Ivy Patel: adding tests to the eval harness now.
Sam Brooks: I'll sketch adapter degraded policies for private airgapped installs.
Rhea Iyer: thanks all, will post RFC link when ready. :rocket:
